responses.question_text: Across the full presentation, how good do the titles, captions, labels, and other content text look and read? Judge whether important content text is visibly present, typography, sizing, weight, spacing, line breaks, contrast, legibility, visual hierarchy, and whether the wording is clear, intentional, and audience-ready rather than sounding like an internal annotation. Do not judge navigation controls or presentation chrome here, and do not judge the placement or styling of non-text elements.

How well designed are the individual scene elements, such as boxes, arrows, icons, illustrations, and diagram nodes? Judge their shapes, proportions, fills, borders, detail, consistency, and overall craft. Do not judge their text, placement, movement, or navigation chrome here.

At a normal wide viewport, how well are the text and visual elements arranged relative to one another? Judge alignment, spacing, grouping, balance, focal points, use of space, and whether anything feels crowded, disconnected, clipped, or unintentionally overlapping. Judge viewport adaptation separately under responsive visual quality.

As you advance through the presentation, how well do the animations and scene changes work? Judge smoothness, pacing, meaningful entrances and exits, continuity of persistent elements, and whether each step visibly evolves the existing scene instead of feeling like an unrelated replacement.

Taken as a whole, how strong is the presentation’s visual identity? Judge its color palette, background treatment, stylistic consistency, brand character, polish, memorability, and whether it feels intentionally designed and finished. Judge the craft of individual scene elements separately.

How clear, discoverable, and visually integrated are the presentation controls and chrome? Judge progress indicators, previous/next controls, table of contents, mode switching, and attribution. findings.message: a trustworthy final full flow is required because bounded final-revision support was not established

technical_adjudication.rationale: User-approved deduction after the deterministic harness was corrected to activate a navigation control the way a pointer does. The candidate stops responding to deck keys once one of its own controls holds focus, which the previous probe could not observe because it activated controls without moving focus.
findings: The previous probe activated a control with element.click(), which does not move focus, so a presentation that suppresses deck keys while a control is focused passed the control-key check. It also skipped the check entirely when present mode exposed no controls, which is where most candidates put their progress controls.

A real-browser replay of the frozen candidate revision 6273deffee378982f5d79e5570c9afa162b434fa measured the defect directly: the arrow key advances the deck from a neutral focus, and does nothing once a navigation control is focused.

demo-navigation-boundaries-and-control-keys is one of five criteria in demo-navigation-and-modes, which carries five points, so the deduction is one point of demo-technical-quality and one point of the official score.
Every other deterministic browser criterion still passes, all four hard gates still pass, and the product verdict is unchanged.
